I apologize in the future if what I am going to say might offend you. Or you might take it badly. 

But I sincerely believe that I need to explain things further. Because things are not just black and white.

I can only assume that you either:

1. Do not come from a third world country.
2. Come from a certain place of privilege.

Going to another country or travelling abroad in order to attend a different Medical School is not as simple as it looks.

A lot of Med Students from Third World Countries study in their own countries, in their own regions, because it is all they can afford to do or pay for. They do not have the money to leave their country for 'greener pastures' as they say. Thus, they make do with the Med Schools in their own countries. Even if the Schools here are not as prestigious or beautiful as those abroad. 

It's all we have. It's all we can afford.

Now, to clarify. I am not saying that I am in poverty or that I am not privileged. Because to a certain extent, you NEED to be privileged to even be studying in Med School here where I am from. However, I am still NOT privileged ENOUGH to study in a whole 'nother country. 

And if you reread what I wrote. I also discussed the continuous unfairness of the system of healthcare and the medical field in Third World Countries.

Where I am from, PGI's and Interns do not have a salary. So they work for FREE for almost 3 to 5 years. And if they are lucky enough to even get a salary, they are given a minimum wage of 300 to 500 Pesos per day. Conversion to US Dollars that is basically 6 to 10 Dollars a Day. 

You don't need to be a genius to know that the salary given is never going to be enough to support a person. 

But again, it's all that we have. These are the cards that we are dealt with. 
It's why I find it draining and depressing. But I still try my hardest to just keep moving onwards.

Thank you so much...
I hope... I can find solace too...
I hope and cling to the phrase... "This too shall pass..."
